subject: Evaluating connection modalities for Finexa private deploy: latency, security, and ops
messages:
From: Luke Thompson <ops@finexa.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Anita Rao <anita.rao@finexa.com>
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment connectivity options - Finexa constraints

Kim,

Thanks for the intro call yesterday. As promised, I wanted to put our constraints and ask in writing so we can get a concrete recommendation from Redwood on connectivity to our VPCs for the private deployment POC. High level:

- Customer: Finexa (regulated financial services)
- Primary goals: end-to-end encryption, minimal blast radius, predictable <15ms latency for API calls, and clear auditability (flow logs, connection time windows).
- Topology: two production VPCs in us-east-1 (separate accounts), one DR VPC in us-west-2.
- Requirements/constraints: no permanent inbound NAT on our customer-facing subnets; strict IP whitelisting preferred; we must preserve internal client IPs where possible for logging; security team will insist on flow logs and key rotation policies.
- Timeline: POC in 3–4 weeks, production decision in 3 months.

Can you summarize tradeoffs between VPC Peering, AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints), and a managed site-to-site IPsec VPN for our use case? Please include operational touchpoints we should expect, typical outage modes, and suggested default for the POC (fastest to stand up vs most production-ready).

I've attached a short matrix with our current network inventory.

—Luke
Luke Thompson
Head of Cloud Ops, Finexa
attach: connectivity_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Luke Thompson <ops@finexa.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity options - Finexa constraints

Luke — thanks for the clear summary and the inventory. Looping in Ben (networking lead), Irene (security), and Jordan (solutions) so we can give a short, pragmatic rec and a POC plan.

Quick TL;DR recommendation for the POC: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) as primary with a temporary site-to-site VPN fallback for the first 6 weeks. Why: PrivateLink gives the cleanest security posture (no cross-account routing changes, endpoint-level access control, and easier IP whitelisting on Redwood side). It preserves customer source IP if you front our endpoint behind a NLB with proxy-protocol or if we use X-Forwarded-For; we’ll document exact behavior in the POC config.

Tradeoffs at a glance (we'll expand below):
- VPC Peering: Lowest network hop latency within region; however, it requires route table management across accounts and broad route exposure if not segmented carefully. Not cross-region friendly (peering is region-limited), and managing IP overlap or on-prem integration is messier.
- PrivateLink (Interface Endpoints): Strong isolation and least blast radius; explicit security principal mapping and interface-level flow logs. Slightly higher per-connection cost (ENI/endpoint hourly + data processing) and needs endpoint DNS handling. Works well cross-account and with strict whitelisting.
- S2S VPN (IPsec): Fast to stand up for POC; good for early validation, but higher operational overhead long term (tunnels flapping, MTU issues, throughput limits depending on customer gateway). Also complicates IP preservation unless using policy-based NAT.

Operational touches we will own: endpoint creation and validation, test harness for latency+tls+egress behavior, sample config for your on-prem/edge firewalls, and standard runbook for failover (PrivateLink down -> route to VPN). Security will want a checklist (flow logs, KMS key rotation, interface endpoint access policies).

I'll ask Ben to add technical tradeoffs and Jordan to draft a POC runbook and timeline.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, Luke Thompson <ops@finexa.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity options - Finexa constraints

Luke / team — adding the technical nuance from a runtime/latency perspective. Important bullets:

- Latency: VPC Peering typically gives the lowest network latency inside the same AZ/region because traffic stays on AWS backbone with minimal extra hops. PrivateLink uses ENIs and an NLB/NAT hop depending on setup, often adding ~1–5ms, though in practice that's usually acceptable for 15ms SLO unless you have tight percentiles.
- IP preservation: By default PrivateLink terminates at the endpoint; the client IP is not always preserved unless you add proxy-protocol or configure a TCP pass-through. We'll provide a sample NLB+proxy-protocol config (see attachment). VPC Peering preserves source IPs natively. VPNs will NAT by default depending on vendor.
- Cross-account routing: Peering means route table entries in each account — operationally heavier and error-prone for large fleets. PrivateLink's security groups and endpoint policies are easier to reason about.
- Cross-region: Peering does not span regions. PrivateLink can be used with inter-region solutions (shared endpoints per region) or use our multi-region deployment. VPN is straightforward cross-region but brings latency and egress costs.
- Failure modes:
  * Peering: human error in route table change can widen blast radius (e.g., accidental 0.0.0.0/0 route).
  * PrivateLink: interface ENI failures are rare; primary risks are DNS misconfiguration and endpoint policy mistakes.
  * VPN: tunnel instability and vendor-specific MTU/fragmentation leading to broken streams are common during peak.
- Cost: PrivateLink has higher per-hour endpoint cost and per-GB processing; peering cost is essentially 0 (within-region) but can increase operational cost for netops. VPN costs depend on gateway device and data transfer.

Attachments: privatelink-interface-config-sample.txt (NLB + proxy protocol example), s2s-vpn-sample-config.txt (sample IPsec phase1/2). I'll also mock an A/B test for latency percentiles during POC and give a runbook for preserving source IPs if you need them in logs.

Ben Carter
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
attach: privatelink-interface-config-sample.txt, s2s-vpn-sample-config.txt

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Luke Thompson <ops@finexa.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed POC plan: PrivateLink primary, VPN fallback, acceptance criteria

Luke — putting the recommended POC plan in one place so your team can review and we can start scheduling. Short plan and acceptance criteria below.

POC objective: Validate connectivity, request/response latency percentiles, source IP/logging fidelity, and operational runbooks before production decision.

Plan (3 weekly sprints):
- Week 0 (prep): exchange account IDs, subnets, and desired CIDR ranges. Set up endpoint IAM roles and endpoint policies. (Owner: Finexa + Redwood solutions)
- Week 1 (build): Redwood creates PrivateLink interface endpoints in us-east-1 (two AZs) and an NLB in our VPC. Finexa validates connectivity from both prod VPCs via endpoint DNS and security group rules.
- Week 2 (validation): Run load tests (10k req/min) to observe p50/p95/p99 latency and error behaviors. Validate flow logs and KMS-based TLS cert rotation in test harness.
- Week 3 (fallback and DR): Stand up managed S2S VPN tunnels to the same VPCs as a fallback. Test failover runbook (cut traffic to VPN, run tests).

Acceptance criteria (must pass to recommend production):
- p95 request latency < 15ms for normal traffic pattern (benchmarked in Week 2).
- Source IPs available in logs or documented mapping in place (we'll provide proxy-protocol option if necessary).
- No critical security gaps in endpoint policies (Irene will run checklist).
- Operational runbook validated with a simulated PrivateLink outage and failover to VPN.

Deliverables we will send by EOD Tue: full endpoint config, runbook, and a templated change request for your NetOps team. If that sounds good we'll schedule a kickoff call Thurs.

Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
